speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with a low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To better assess your condition, have you noticed any specific patterns to your rash, such as it spreading quickly or appearing in crops? Additionally, have you experienced any joint pain, swollen lymph nodes, or a sore throat recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Scarlet fever (Group A Streptococcus). The clinical presentation of a pruritic rash spreading from the trunk to extremities, a low-grade fever, and specifically a facial rash sparing the perioral area is classic for scarlet fever, which often follows a viral prodrome of fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. We should confirm this with a throat examination and a rapid strep test. REQUEST TEST: Throat_Culture; REQUEST TEST: Rapid_Strep_Test.
